6.	X has four chapters and only 35 verses. It takes its name from its first word, which is a question word. It opens with questions like, “by whose will does the mind think? By whose command does the breath function? By whose wish do people speak?” The most famous passage of this text tells the story of how the dEvas become puffed with pride after a victory and brahman appears disguised as a yaksha to humble them. The gods are shocked when agni and vAyu fail in their attempts to bully the yaksha, and the goddess umA explains to indra that the dEvas get their powers not from themselves but from brahman, answering the opening question. ID X (10 points).
